text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your infant's recurrent stridor and wheezing, could you please tell me the baby's age and if these symptoms worsen during feeding or crying?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. The fact that symptoms worsen with neck flexion is highly suggestive of a vascular ring anomaly. Does the stridor or wheezing change or improve when you gently extend the baby's neck?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The relief with neck extension strongly supports a diagnosis of a vascular ring, likely a double aortic arch or right aortic arch with aberrant left subclavian artery. I will order imaging to confirm the anatomy and rule out other causes.
